* {{IPA|en|/stɔp/|a=SSB,AU,Scotland}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-stop.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/stɑp/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-stop.ogg|a=GenAm}}
* {{IPA|en|/stɒp/|a=CA}}
* {{IPA|en|/stɒp/|[stɔ̟p]|a=NZ}}
* {{IPA|en|/(ɪ)sʈɔp/|/(ɪ)sʈɑp/<a:father-bother>|a=Indic}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)tewp-}}
{{ety|en|id=cease moving|:inh|enm:stoppen}}
From {{inh|en|enm|stoppen}}, {{m|enm|stoppien}}, from {{inh|en|ang|stoppian|t=to stop, close}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*stoppōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*stuppōną|t=to stop, close}}, {{m|gem-pro|*stuppijaną|t=to push, pierce, prick}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)tewp-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*(s)tewb-|t=to push; stick}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*(s)tew-|t=to bump; impact; butt; push; beat; strike; hit}}.

Cognate with {{cog|stq|stopje||to stop, block}}, {{cog|fy|stopje||to stop}}, {{cog|nl|stoppen||to stop}}, {{cog|nds|stoppen||to stop}}, {{cog|de|stopfen||to be filling, stuff}}, {{cog|de|stoppen||to stop}}, {{cog|da,nb|stoppe||to stop}}, {{cog|is,nn,sv|stoppa||to stop}}, {{cog|gmh|stupfen}}, {{m|gmh|stüpfen||to pierce}}. More at [[stuff]], [[stump]].

Alternative etymology derives Proto-West Germanic *''stoppōn'' from an assumed {{cog|la-vul|*stūpāre}}, {{m|la|*stuppāre||to stop up with tow}}, from {{m|la|stūpa}}, {{m|la|stīpa}}, {{m|la|stuppa||tow, flax, oakum}}, from {{cog|grc|στύπη}}, {{m|grc|στύππη||tow, flax, oakum}}. This derivation, however, is doubtful, as the earliest instances of the Germanic verb do not carry the meaning of "stuff, stop with tow". Rather, these senses developed later in response to influence from similar sounding words in Latin and Romance.<ref>The Century Dictionary and Cyclopedia, "stop".</ref>

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{senseid|en|cease moving}}{{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[cease]] moving.
#: {{ux|en|I '''stopped''' at the traffic lights.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} Not to [[continue]].
#: {{ux|en|The riots '''stopped''' when police moved in.}}
#: {{ux|en|Soon the rain will '''stop'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=5|passage=Then everybody once more knelt, and soon the blessing was pronounced. The choir and the clergy trooped out slowly, {{...}}, down the nave to the western door. {{...}} At a seemingly immense distance the surpliced group '''stopped''' to say the last prayer.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause (something) to cease moving or [[progressing]].
#: {{ux|en|The sight of the armed men '''stopped''' him in his tracks.}}
#: {{ux|en|This guy is a fraudster. I need to '''stop''' the cheque I wrote him.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838
|page=13 (Technology Quarterly)
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/technology-quarterly/21578516-transport-new-train-technologies-are-less-visible-and-spread-less-quickly Ideas coming down the track]
|passage=A “moving platform” scheme{{...}}is more technologically ambitious than maglev trains even though it relies on conventional rails.{{...}}This set-up solves several problems […]. '''Stopping''' high-speed trains wastes energy and time, so why not simply slow them down enough for a moving platform to pull alongside?}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[cease]]; to no longer continue.
#: {{ant|en|keep}}
#: {{ux|en|One of the wrestlers suddenly '''stopped''' fighting.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause (something) to [[come to an end]].
#: {{ux|en|The referees '''stopped''' the fight.}}
# {{lb|en|causative|transitive}} To [[interrupt]], [[prevent]] or end the activity of someone or something. {{+obj|en|dirobj + gerund<qq:chiefly UK> / dirobj + :from + gerund<qq:chiefly US>}}
#: {{ux|en|Don't let me '''stop''' you working.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[close]] or [[block]] an [[opening]].
#: {{ux|en|He '''stopped''' the wound with gauze.}}
#: {{ux|en|Rotten leaves and branches have '''stopped''' the gutter.}}
#: {{ux|en|I've had the cracks in the wall '''stopped''' with mortar by the builders.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive|photography|often with "up" or "down"}} To [[adjust]] the [[aperture]] of a [[camera]] [[lens]].
#: {{ux|en|To achieve maximum depth of field, he '''stopped''' down to an f-stop of 22.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[stay]]; to spend a short [[time]]; to reside or [[tarry]] temporarily.
#: {{ux|en|to '''stop''' with a friend}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''stopped''' for two weeks at the inn.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''stopped''' at his friend's house before continuing with his drive.}}
#* {{RQ:Blackmore Springhaven|volume=I|chapter=The Maroon|page=68|passage=Springhaven had done so well last week, that this week it meant to do still better, by '''stopping''' at home till the money was gone, and making short work afterwards.}}
# {{lb|en|music}} To regulate the sounds of (musical strings, etc.) by pressing them against the [[fingerboard]] with the finger, or otherwise shortening the vibrating part.
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[punctuate]].
#* {{RQ:Landor Imaginary Conversations|edition=2nd|volume=II|conv=XIII|chapter=[[w:Vittorio Alfieri|{{quote-gloss|Vittorio}} Alfieri]] and Salomon, the Florentine Jew|page=415|passage=[[w:Francesco Guicciardini|{{quote-gloss|Francesco}} Guicciardini]], if his sentences were properly '''stopt''', would be found in general both full and concise, whatever may be asserted to the contrary by the fastidious and inattentive.}}
# {{lb|en|nautical}} To make [[fast]]; to [[stopper]].
# {{sid|en|phon-verb}} {{lb|en|phonetics|transitive}} To [[pronounce]] (a [[phoneme]]) as a {{l|en|stop|id=phon-noun}}.
#: {{ux|en|[[''th''-'''stopping''']]}}
# {{lb|en|finance|transitive}} To [[delay]] the purchase or sale of (a [[stock]]) while agreeing the [[price]] for later.
# To take out of service for [[repair]], [[servicing]] or [[examination]].
# To quit partaking in the use of or participation in (something).
#: {{ux|en|She '''stopped''' heroin last year.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''stopped''' football to focus on acting.}}

=====Usage notes=====
* This is a [[catenative verb]] that takes the ''gerund [[-ing]]'' to indicate the ending action (''stop thinking''), or the ''to'' infinitive to indicate the purpose of the interruption (''stop to think''). See [[Appendix:English_catenative_verbs#Difference_in_meaning|Appendix:English catenative verbs]] for more information.
* When used causatively, the verb can either be followed directly by its dependent clause (for example, ''to stop them exploding'') or take a helper word, usually ''[[from]]'', before the clause (''to stop them from exploding'').  The former usage is more common in Britain, and the latter usage  more common in America.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|station}} A (usually marked) [[place]] where [[bus]]es, [[tram]]s or [[train]]s [[halt]] to let [[passenger]]s get on and off, usually smaller than a [[station]].
#: Related terms: [[halt]], [[station]].
#: {{ux|en|They agreed to meet at the bus '''stop'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|action of stopping}} An action of stopping; [[interruption]] of travel.
#: {{ux|en|That '''stop''' was not planned.}}
#* {{RQ:Defoe Plague Year|passage=It is {{...}} doubtful {{...}} whether it contributed anything to the '''stop''' of the infection.}}
#* {{RQ:Newton Opticks
|passage=Occult qualities put a '''stop''' to the improvement of natural philosophy.}}
#* {{RQ:Locke Education|107
|passage=It is a great step toward the mastery of our desires to give this '''stop''' to them.}}
# That which stops, impedes, or obstructs; an [[obstacle]]; an [[impediment]].
#* {{RQ:Daniel Civil Wars|passage=A fatal '''stop''' trauerst their headlong course}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1729|author={{w|John Rogers (priest)|John Rogers}}|title=The Advantages of conversing with good Men
|passage=So melancholy a prospect should inspire us with zeal to oppose some '''stop''' to the rising torrent.}}
# A [[device]] intended to [[block]] the path of a moving object
#: {{usex|en|door '''stop'''}}
## {{lb|en|engineering}} A device, or piece, as a pin, block, pawl, etc., for arresting or limiting motion, or for determining the position to which another part shall be brought.
## {{lb|en|architecture}} A member, plain or moulded, formed of a separate piece and fixed to a jamb, against which a door or window shuts.
# {{sid|en|phon-noun}} {{lb|en|phonetics}} A [[consonant]] [[sound]] in which the [[passage]] of [[air]] is [[temporarily]] blocked by the [[lips]], [[tongue]], or [[glottis]].
#: {{syn|en|plosive|occlusive}}
# A symbol used for purposes of punctuation and representing a pause or separating clauses, particularly a [[full stop]], [[comma]], [[colon]] or [[semicolon]].
# {{lb|en|music}} A [[knob]] or [[pin]] used to regulate the flow of air in an [[organ]].
#: {{ux|en|The organ is loudest when all the '''stops''' are pulled.}}
# {{lb|en|music}} One of the vent-holes in a [[wind instrument]], or the place on the wire of a [[stringed instrument]], by the stopping or pressing of which certain notes are produced.
# {{lb|en|tennis}} A very [[short]] [[shot]] which touches the ground close behind the [[net]] and is intended to bounce as little as possible.
# {{lb|en|football}} A [[save]]; preventing the opposition from scoring a goal.
#* {{quote-web|en|date=May 15 2021|author=Phil McNulty|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57055571|title=Chelsea 0-1 Leicester|passage=The Foxes were indebted to two crucial saves from keeper Kasper Schmeichel, who turned former Leicester defender Ben Chilwell's header on to a post then produced an even better '''stop''' to turn Mason Mount's powerful shot wide.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261001132304/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57055571|archivedate=1 October 2026}}
# {{lb|en|zoology}} The [[depression]] in a dog’s face between the skull and the nasal bones.
#: {{ux|en|The '''stop''' in a bulldog's face is very marked.}}
# A marking on a rabbit's hind foot.
#: {{ux|en|The American Rabbit Breeders Association holds that the '''stops''' of a [[Dutch rabbit]] should be white from the toes to one third of the way along the foot.}}
# {{lb|en|photography}} A part of a [[photographic]] system that reduces the amount of [[light]].
# {{lb|en|photography}} A unit of [[exposure]] corresponding to a doubling of the [[brightness]] of an image.
# {{lb|en|photography}} An [[f-stop]].
# The [[diaphragm]] used in optical instruments to cut off the marginal portions of a beam of light passing through lenses.
# {{lb|en|fencing}} A [[coup d'arret]], or [[stop thrust]].
# {{lb|en|UK|grammar|informal}} {{ellipsis of|en|full stop}}.

{{col-top|2|cog}}
